questions.title: Course Schedule III
questions.primary_pattern: Greedy by deadline + max-heap regret replacement
questions.trigger: Maximise the number of items finishable before individual deadlines.
questions.why: Sort by deadline, take everything, and when infeasible drop the longest course taken so far.
questions.alternatives: DP over (index, elapsed time).
questions.selection_reason: The regret-replacement heap is a distinct greedy shape and is easy to miss entirely.

questions.title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
questions.primary_pattern: Monotonic deque over prefix sums
questions.trigger: Shortest subarray with sum >= K, but values may be negative so the window is not monotone.
questions.why: Keep prefix sums in an increasing deque; pop from the front when P[i]-P[front] >= k, pop from the back to keep it increasing.
questions.alternatives: Naive sliding window (wrong with negatives); balanced BST over prefix sums.
questions.selection_reason: The canonical proof that 'sum + negatives' kills the window - the exact trigger split in the index.

questions.title: Combination Sum IV
questions.primary_pattern: Order-sensitive unbounded counting DP (permutations)
questions.trigger: Counts SEQUENCES, not multisets, so the same numbers in another order count twice.
questions.why: dp[t] = sum over nums of dp[t-num], with the target loop outside and the item loop inside.
questions.alternatives: Recursion with memoisation on the remaining target.
questions.selection_reason: The loop-order distinction against coin-change is the single most confusable point in knapsack DP.

questions.title: Magnetic Force Between Two Balls
questions.primary_pattern: Binary search on the answer + greedy feasibility
questions.trigger: Maximise the minimum gap - a maximin objective with a monotone feasibility predicate.
questions.why: Sort, binary search the gap d, and greedily place balls at least d apart to test whether m fit.
questions.alternatives: Parametric search; DP over placements (too slow).
questions.selection_reason: Clean maximin case where the greedy check is the part that must be invented.

questions.title: Russian Doll Envelopes
questions.primary_pattern: Longest increasing subsequence after a sorting trick
questions.trigger: Two-dimensional nesting with strict inequality in both dimensions.
questions.why: Sort by width ascending and height DESCENDING on ties, then run the O(n log n) LIS on heights.
questions.alternatives: O(n^2) DP over pairs; segment tree over coordinates.
questions.selection_reason: The tie-breaking direction is the whole insight, and it is invisible until you try to break it.

questions.title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
questions.primary_pattern: Offline queries + sort + min-heap of active intervals
questions.trigger: Per-query output asking for the SMALLEST interval covering each query point.
questions.why: Sort queries and intervals by coordinate; push intervals whose start has passed, lazily pop those that ended, and read the heap's smallest length.
questions.alternatives: Segment tree over compressed coordinates; merge-sort-tree.
questions.selection_reason: Verbatim match for the index's 'point queries + best covering interval' line.

questions.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
questions.primary_pattern: Minimum spanning tree on a complete graph (Prim)
questions.trigger: Connect all nodes at minimum total cost with a dense implicit edge set.
questions.why: Prim's algorithm on the implicit complete graph in O(n^2), or Kruskal over all pairs.
questions.alternatives: Kruskal with sorted edges and union-find.
questions.selection_reason: Names no graph at all; the MST trigger has to come from 'connect everything, cheapest'.

questions.title: 132 Pattern
questions.primary_pattern: Monotonic decreasing stack scanned right to left
questions.trigger: Find i<j<k with a[i] < a[k] < a[j] - an ordering constraint across three separated indices.
questions.why: Sweep from the right maintaining a decreasing stack; popped values become the best possible 'a[k]' candidate.
questions.alternatives: Prefix minimum for a[i] plus an ordered set for a[k]; O(n^2) over j.
questions.selection_reason: Non-obvious stack usage where the discarded elements, not the stack, carry the answer.

questions.title: Car Fleet
questions.primary_pattern: Sort by position, monotonic stack of arrival times
questions.trigger: Cars merge and never split, so a slower car ahead absorbs everything catching up to it.
questions.why: Sort by descending position; a fleet forms whenever the current arrival time exceeds the stack top's.
questions.alternatives: Scan from the front tracking a running maximum arrival time.
questions.selection_reason: Physical story that hides a next-greater-element scan; very easy to misread as simulation.

questions.title: Maximum Number of K-Divisible Components
questions.primary_pattern: Post-order DFS on a tree, cutting edges when a subtree sum is divisible
questions.trigger: Split a tree into the maximum number of parts whose value sums are each divisible by k.
questions.why: Post-order accumulate subtree sums mod k; whenever a subtree's residue is zero, cut that edge and count a component.
questions.alternatives: Iterative peeling of leaves with accumulated residues.
questions.selection_reason: Combines the index's tree-splitting line with modular subtree accumulation.

questions.title: Possible Bipartition
questions.primary_pattern: Two-colouring by BFS/DFS
questions.trigger: Mutual-dislike constraints are exactly 'these two must be on different sides'.
questions.why: BFS colouring each component; a conflict on an existing colour proves impossibility.
questions.alternatives: Union-find with parity, or a union-find of size 2n.
questions.selection_reason: The bipartite trigger hidden behind a social-grouping story.

questions.title: Repeated DNA Sequences
questions.primary_pattern: Rolling hash / fixed-window signature over a small alphabet
questions.trigger: Find repeated fixed-length substrings over a 4-letter alphabet in a long string.
questions.why: Encode each window as a 2-bits-per-character integer and roll it forward, storing seen codes in a set.
questions.alternatives: Store the raw substrings in a hash set (simpler, more memory).
questions.selection_reason: Fixed-size window plus signature hashing, with an alphabet small enough to make bit packing natural.

questions.title: Shifting Letters II
questions.primary_pattern: Difference array, prefix sum once at the end
questions.trigger: Many range updates, and the answer is only read after all of them are applied.
questions.why: Add +/-1 at the range boundaries, prefix-sum once, then apply the shift modulo 26.
questions.alternatives: Segment tree with lazy propagation (correct but far heavier).
questions.selection_reason: Range-update / query-at-end with a modular twist, without the overused booking framing.

questions.title: Single Number III
questions.primary_pattern: XOR everything + isolate a differing bit
questions.trigger: Everything appears twice except TWO numbers, so a single XOR leaves their combination.
questions.why: XOR all to get a^b, take the lowest set bit, and partition the array on it to XOR each group separately.
questions.alternatives: Hash-map counting (O(n) extra space).
questions.selection_reason: The partitioning step is what the plain XOR trick never prepares you for.

questions.title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String II
questions.primary_pattern: Stack of (character, run length)
questions.trigger: Removing a run of k identical characters closes the gap and can trigger further removals.
questions.why: Push (char, count) pairs; increment on a match and pop when the count reaches k.
questions.alternatives: Repeated scanning passes until the string stabilises (O(n^2)).
questions.selection_reason: The clearest statement of 'adjacent elements cancel, gap closes, cascades'.

questions.title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
questions.primary_pattern: Min-heap of list heads + running maximum
questions.trigger: The range must contain at least one element from each of k sorted lists.
questions.why: Keep one pointer per list in a min-heap alongside the current maximum; advance the minimum and track the best span.
questions.alternatives: Merge everything into one labelled sorted array and run a variable window over labels.
questions.selection_reason: K-way merge and sliding window are the same walk here - a genuinely instructive overlap.

questions.title: Replace Non-Coprime Numbers in Array
questions.primary_pattern: Stack with cascading merges + GCD/LCM
questions.trigger: Adjacent elements merge when they share a factor, and the merged value can trigger further merges leftward.
questions.why: Push onto a stack; while gcd(top, cur) > 1, pop and replace cur with lcm(top, cur).
questions.alternatives: Repeated left-to-right passes until stable (too slow).
questions.selection_reason: Number theory driving a stack cascade - two sections of the index in a single statement.

questions.title: Single-Threaded CPU
questions.primary_pattern: Event-ordered simulation + min-heap by priority
questions.trigger: Repeatedly take the best available item, where availability changes with time.
questions.why: Sort by arrival, push everything available into a heap keyed by (duration, index), and jump time forward when idle.
questions.alternatives: Two-pointer over sorted arrivals with the same heap.
questions.selection_reason: The index's 'schedule by priority' line, with an idle-time jump that most first attempts miss.

questions.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
questions.primary_pattern: Min-heap over a frontier of candidate pairs
questions.trigger: Smallest k sums from an implicit sorted matrix of pairs that must not be materialised.
questions.why: Seed the heap with the first row's pairs and, on each pop, push only the next candidate in that row.
questions.alternatives: Binary search on the sum value with a counting predicate.
questions.selection_reason: The frontier-expansion idea behind merging k sorted lists, stated without any lists in sight.

questions.title: Minimum Initial Energy to Finish Tasks
questions.primary_pattern: Exchange argument - sort by (minimum - actual) descending
questions.trigger: Each task has a consumption and a higher threshold, and only the ORDER is free.
questions.why: Sort by (minimum - actual) descending and accumulate; swapping two adjacent tasks proves the rule.
questions.alternatives: Binary search the starting energy with a greedy feasibility check.
questions.selection_reason: Verbatim match for the index's 'minimum starting resource' line.

questions.title: Distribute Coins in Binary Tree
questions.primary_pattern: Post-order DFS returning a signed surplus
questions.trigger: Coins move along edges, and each edge's traffic is decided entirely by its subtree.
questions.why: Return (subtree coins - subtree nodes) upward and add |flow| on every edge to the answer.
questions.alternatives: Same recursion phrased as a flow-conservation argument.
questions.selection_reason: Purest 'children before parent' problem - the return value IS the algorithm.

questions.title: Maximum Width Ramp
questions.primary_pattern: Monotonic stack of candidate left endpoints, scanned from the right
questions.trigger: Maximise j-i subject to a[i] <= a[j] - a distance objective under an inequality.
questions.why: Push a strictly decreasing stack of candidate i's, then sweep j from the right popping while a[j] >= stack top.
questions.alternatives: Sort indices by value and track the minimum index seen; binary search over a decreasing prefix-min array.
questions.selection_reason: Exactly the index's 'max distance + inequality, keep only useful candidates' line.

questions.title: Minimum Cost For Tickets
questions.primary_pattern: Forward DP where every prefix is an answer
questions.trigger: Choices at a day affect a forward span of days, and the cost must be known at each prefix.
questions.why: dp[d] = min over pass types of dp[max(0, d-span)] + cost, iterating days forward.
questions.alternatives: DP over travel-day indices with binary search for the next uncovered day.
questions.selection_reason: Direct instance of the index's 'answer needed at every prefix, build forward' line.

questions.title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
questions.primary_pattern: Binary search on the answer + linear greedy check
questions.trigger: 'Minimum day such that it becomes possible' - feasibility is monotone in the day.
questions.why: Binary search the day, then scan counting maximal runs of bloomed flowers to test whether m bouquets fit.
questions.alternatives: Sort days and add flowers incrementally with union-find over adjacent runs.
questions.selection_reason: Clean minimum-X-such-that formulation where the check, not the search, carries the work.

questions.title: Find the Longest Substring Containing Vowels in Even Counts
questions.primary_pattern: Prefix XOR bitmask + first-occurrence hash map
questions.trigger: Only the PARITY of five counts matters, so the whole state fits in 5 bits.
questions.why: Track a 5-bit parity mask; equal masks at i and j mean every vowel appears an even number of times in between.
questions.alternatives: Prefix counts per vowel with pairwise comparison (O(n^2)).
questions.selection_reason: Teaches state compression into a bitmask, then the standard first-seen prefix lookup.

questions.title: Jump Game VI
questions.primary_pattern: DP + monotonic deque for a windowed max
questions.trigger: dp[i] may only jump from the previous k indices, so each transition needs a windowed maximum.
questions.why: dp[i] = a[i] + max(dp[i-k..i-1]); a decreasing deque yields that maximum in O(1) amortised.
questions.alternatives: Max-heap with lazy deletion; segment tree over dp values.
questions.selection_reason: Windows the DP transition rather than the array - a shape plain sliding-window practice never produces.

questions.title: Maximum Number of Removable Characters
questions.primary_pattern: Binary search on the answer + subsequence check
questions.trigger: 'Largest k such that it still works' with a cheap O(n) validity test.
questions.why: Feasibility is monotone in k; mark the first k removals and verify p is still a subsequence of s.
questions.alternatives: Incremental union-find over restorations processed backwards.
questions.selection_reason: The monotonicity is over a set of removals, not a numeric quantity - a much harder trigger to spot.

questions.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
questions.primary_pattern: Bellman-Ford with a bounded number of relaxation rounds
questions.trigger: Cheapest path subject to a hard cap on the number of edges used.
questions.why: Relax all edges k+1 times over a snapshot of the previous round's distances.
questions.alternatives: Dijkstra over (node, stops) states; layered BFS with a cost array.
questions.selection_reason: The hop limit is what breaks plain Dijkstra - the reason Bellman-Ford exists in the table.

questions.title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
questions.primary_pattern: Weighted interval scheduling DP + binary search
questions.trigger: Non-overlapping intervals with WEIGHTS, so the count-based greedy no longer applies.
questions.why: Sort by end time; dp[i] = max(skip, profit + dp[last job ending <= start]) with the predecessor found by binary search.
questions.alternatives: DP over a heap of running best profits; segment tree over coordinates.
questions.selection_reason: The exact point where 'sort by end and take greedily' stops working - a high-value discrimination.

questions.title: Video Stitching
questions.primary_pattern: Greedy interval covering of [0, T]
questions.trigger: Cover an entire time range using the fewest given intervals.
questions.why: Track the farthest reach for each left endpoint and extend coverage greedily, counting each extension.
questions.alternatives: DP over positions; BFS treating reachable ranges as layers.
questions.selection_reason: Verbatim instance of the index's 'minimum intervals to cover [0,T]' line.

questions.title: Swim in Rising Water
questions.primary_pattern: Minimax path - Dijkstra, or binary search + BFS, or Kruskal union-find
questions.trigger: Minimise the maximum cell value along a path in a grid.
questions.why: Dijkstra where a path's cost is the running maximum; equivalently, add cells in increasing value until start and end connect.
questions.alternatives: Binary search the threshold with a reachability BFS.
questions.selection_reason: Three fully valid patterns converge; excellent for practising the choice rather than the code.

questions.title: Shortest Bridge
questions.primary_pattern: Flood fill to label one component, then multi-source BFS
questions.trigger: Two components, and you need the shortest gap between them.
questions.why: DFS/BFS to collect every cell of the first island, push them all as BFS sources, and expand until the second island is hit.
questions.alternatives: BFS from every cell of one island independently.
questions.selection_reason: Two distinct grid patterns composed in sequence, which is what makes it worth practising.

questions.title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to Limit
questions.primary_pattern: Sliding window + monotonic max deque + monotonic min deque
questions.trigger: Longest window whose validity depends on both the window max and the window min.
questions.why: Maintain a decreasing deque for max and an increasing deque for min; shrink while max-min > limit.
questions.alternatives: Ordered multiset (TreeMap) of the window; two heaps with lazy deletion.
questions.selection_reason: The textbook case where one deque is not enough - directly named in the index.

questions.title: Exclusive Time of Functions
questions.primary_pattern: Stack of active frames with a running timestamp
questions.trigger: Nested calls where a parent's own time excludes the time spent inside its children.
questions.why: Push on start, and on end pop while crediting elapsed time to the top frame and charging it against its parent.
questions.alternatives: Recursive parsing of the log into a call tree.
questions.selection_reason: The 'most-recent-first / undo' stack semantics, where the bookkeeping rather than the structure is the difficulty.

questions.title: Serialize and Deserialize BST
questions.primary_pattern: Pre-order serialisation exploiting the BST bound invariant
questions.trigger: Round-tripping a tree, with the BST property available to remove null markers.
questions.why: Emit pre-order values; rebuild recursively using (min, max) bounds to decide where each value belongs.
questions.alternatives: Pre-order with explicit null markers; store both pre-order and in-order.
questions.selection_reason: Rebuilding from bounds instead of markers is the part the generic version never teaches.

questions.title: Two City Scheduling
questions.primary_pattern: Exchange argument - sort by the pairwise difference
questions.trigger: Exactly half must go each way, and swapping two people exposes the ordering rule.
questions.why: Sort by costA - costB and send the first half to A.
questions.alternatives: Min-cost flow / assignment DP over (index, count sent to A).
questions.selection_reason: Textbook exchange argument stated plainly enough that the proof is visible.

questions.title: Special Array With X Elements Greater Than or Equal X
questions.primary_pattern: Counting / binary search on a self-referential predicate
questions.trigger: x must equal the number of elements >= x - the answer is defined by a count of itself.
questions.why: Sort (or bucket-count) and test each candidate x from 1..n; the predicate is monotone.
questions.alternatives: Counting-sort with a suffix sum over value buckets.
questions.selection_reason: Easy where the entire difficulty is realising the predicate is monotone and the search space is the answer.

questions.title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
questions.primary_pattern: 2D DP over intervals, filled by increasing length
questions.trigger: One string with palindromic substructure, so the state is a substring and the base case is the diagonal.
questions.why: dp[i][j] = dp[i+1][j-1] + 2 on a character match, else max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
questions.alternatives: LCS of s with its reverse.
questions.selection_reason: The reference shape for the index's palindromic-substructure line, including the fill order.

questions.title: Simplified Fractions
questions.primary_pattern: Coprimality via GCD over an enumerated pair space
secondary_patterns: Brute force with a divisibility filter
questions.trigger: Every fraction must be in lowest terms, i.e. numerator and denominator coprime, with n small enough to enumerate all pairs.
questions.why: Enumerate denominators and numerators and keep the pairs with gcd == 1; the count of kept pairs per denominator is exactly phi(denominator).
questions.alternatives: Sieve-style totient precomputation when only the COUNT is needed rather than the list.
questions.selection_reason: Reaches the index's coprime/totient line through a statement that names neither, so the trigger has to be recognised rather than read off the title.

questions.title: Count Triplets That Can Form Two Arrays of Equal XOR
questions.primary_pattern: Prefix XOR + the observation that the split point is free
questions.trigger: Two adjacent segments must have equal XOR, and the split between them can sit anywhere.
questions.why: Equal XOR means prefix[i] == prefix[k+1]; every j in between works, so count pairs and weight by distance.
questions.alternatives: O(n^2) over (i, k) with a running XOR.
questions.selection_reason: Prefix reasoning transplanted from sums to XOR, plus a counting argument that removes a dimension.

questions.title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
questions.primary_pattern: Common binary prefix of the range endpoints
questions.trigger: The range can span up to 2^31 values, so the numbers cannot be iterated at all.
questions.why: The AND over a range equals the shared high-order prefix of left and right; shift both right until they meet.
questions.alternatives: Brian Kernighan: repeatedly clear the lowest set bit of right while it exceeds left.
questions.selection_reason: Textbook case of the index's 'the input cannot be iterated' signal resolving to pure bit reasoning.

questions.title: Smallest String With Swaps
questions.primary_pattern: Union-find components + sort within each component
questions.trigger: Swaps are given as pairs but can be composed arbitrarily, so each component is freely permutable.
questions.why: Union the swap pairs, then sort each component's characters into its sorted index positions.
questions.alternatives: DFS to collect components; equivalent connected-component labelling.
questions.selection_reason: The leap from 'pairwise swaps' to 'any permutation within a component' is the entire problem.

questions.title: Total Hamming Distance
questions.primary_pattern: Per-bit column counting
questions.trigger: Sums a pairwise statistic over all pairs, but bits are independent of one another.
questions.why: For each of the 32 bit positions, the contribution is (count of ones) * (count of zeros).
questions.alternatives: O(n^2) pairwise XOR with a popcount.
questions.selection_reason: Decomposing an aggregate along bit columns is a reusable idea well beyond this problem.

questions.title: Sum of Subarray Minimums
questions.primary_pattern: Monotonic stack for contribution counting
questions.trigger: Sums a statistic over ALL subarrays, so each element's total contribution must be counted directly.
questions.why: For each element find the previous-smaller and next-smaller spans; it is the minimum of left*right subarrays.
questions.alternatives: O(n^2) enumeration; divide and conquer on the minimum.
questions.selection_reason: The contribution technique - the step from 'next smaller element' to actually using it.

questions.title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
questions.primary_pattern: Union-find over shared rows and columns
questions.trigger: Removability cascades, and the answer is n minus the number of connected components.
questions.why: Union each stone with its row key and column key; count components over the used keys.
questions.alternatives: DFS/BFS on a graph built from shared coordinates.
questions.selection_reason: Both the graph and the 'n - components' reformulation must be invented from a removal story.

questions.title: Queue Reconstruction by Height
questions.primary_pattern: Greedy insertion after sorting by height
questions.trigger: Each person's constraint counts only people at least as tall, so taller people are placed first.
questions.why: Sort by height descending and count ascending, then insert each person at index k.
questions.alternatives: Binary indexed tree over free slots for an O(n log n) placement.
questions.selection_reason: Correctness hinges on why later insertions cannot invalidate earlier ones.

questions.title: Step-By-Step Directions From a Binary Tree Node to Another
questions.primary_pattern: Lowest common ancestor + root-to-node paths
questions.trigger: A path between two nodes in a rooted tree always goes up to their LCA and back down.
questions.why: Find the root paths for both nodes, strip the common prefix, replace the first leg with 'U's.
questions.alternatives: Locate the LCA first, then search downwards for each target.
questions.selection_reason: Applies LCA rather than merely computing it, which is where the recognition actually matters.

questions.title: Open the Lock
questions.primary_pattern: BFS over an implicit state graph
questions.trigger: Minimum number of moves with uniform cost over states, not over an explicit graph.
questions.why: Treat each 4-digit combination as a node with 8 neighbours; BFS from '0000' avoiding deadends.
questions.alternatives: Bidirectional BFS; A* with a digit-distance heuristic.
questions.selection_reason: The graph is never given - recognising that states are nodes is the whole trigger.

questions.title: Minimum Height Trees
questions.primary_pattern: Topological peeling of leaves inward
questions.trigger: Asks for the best ROOTS of a tree, which are its one or two centres.
questions.why: Repeatedly strip all current leaves; the last one or two nodes remaining are the answers.
questions.alternatives: Two BFS passes to find the diameter, then take its midpoint(s).
questions.selection_reason: Kahn's algorithm applied to an undirected tree - a shape most people only meet on DAGs.

questions.title: Minimum Cost to Hire K Workers
questions.primary_pattern: Sort by ratio + max-heap of quality
questions.trigger: Pay is proportional within a group, so the group's cost is driven by its worst ratio.
questions.why: Sort by wage/quality; sweep, keeping the k smallest qualities in a max-heap, and score at each ratio.
questions.alternatives: Enumerate every worker as the ratio setter with a selection over the rest.
questions.selection_reason: The index's 'greedy by ratio' line combined with a heap - two triggers that must both fire.

questions.title: Path Sum III
questions.primary_pattern: Prefix sum + hash map, applied on a root-to-node path
questions.trigger: Counts downward paths summing to a target on a tree, with negative values allowed.
questions.why: Carry a running root-to-node prefix sum in a map; on entering a node add curr-target, and decrement the map on exit.
questions.alternatives: O(n^2) DFS from every node.
questions.selection_reason: Transplants an array trigger onto a tree - exactly the cross-pattern recognition being drilled.

questions.title: Number of Ways to Reorder Array to Get Same BST
questions.primary_pattern: Divide and conquer + binomial coefficients modulo a prime
questions.trigger: Counts interleavings of two independent sequences that preserve a fixed structure.
questions.why: Recurse on the left and right subtrees and multiply by C(l+r, l), using precomputed factorials and modular inverses.
questions.alternatives: Memoised recursion over sorted index sets with Pascal's triangle.
questions.selection_reason: The index's 'combinatorics with a modulus' line applied on top of a BST insight.

questions.title: Uncrossed Lines
questions.primary_pattern: Longest common subsequence in disguise
questions.trigger: Connections may not cross, which forces the chosen pairs into increasing index order in both arrays.
questions.why: Non-crossing + increasing in both sequences is precisely LCS; dp[i][j] over the two arrays.
questions.alternatives: LIS on matched index pairs.
questions.selection_reason: Geometric statement of a known recurrence - pure recognition, no new technique.

questions.title: Amount of Time for Binary Tree to Be Infected
questions.primary_pattern: Convert the tree to an undirected graph, then BFS from a source
questions.trigger: Spreading reaches parents as well as children, so the tree must be traversed as a graph.
questions.why: Build a parent map (or adjacency list) and BFS from the start node; the answer is the last layer index.
questions.alternatives: Single DFS returning depth and a burn time simultaneously.
questions.selection_reason: Rehearses 'a tree is a graph' - the child-only recursion silently gives the wrong answer.

questions.title: Minimum Cost Tree From Leaf Values
questions.primary_pattern: Monotonic increasing stack (greedy removal of local minima)
questions.trigger: Build a tree over an array whose cost involves the maximum of each side - looks like classic interval DP.
questions.why: Repeatedly remove the smallest element, paying it times its smaller neighbour; a monotonic stack does this in O(n).
questions.alternatives: O(n^3) interval DP dp[i][j] with a max table - correct and much easier to see.
questions.selection_reason: Deliberate two-approach trap: interval DP is right, but the stack is the intended insight.

questions.title: Min Cost to Connect Ropes
questions.primary_pattern: Min-heap, repeatedly combine the two smallest
questions.trigger: 'Minimum total cost to combine all items', where every merge cost equals the combined size.
questions.why: Always merge the two smallest current items; a min-heap supplies them in O(log n).
questions.alternatives: Sorting once is NOT sufficient, because merged values re-enter the pool.
questions.selection_reason: Fills the index's 'minimum cost to combine all items' line, whose LeetCode version is paywalled; also the correct-greedy counterpart to the merge-stones trap.

questions.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
questions.primary_pattern: Backtracking with pruning, or DP over a subset bitmask
questions.trigger: Partition into k equal-sum groups with n <= 16 - the constraint size openly permits exponential search.
questions.why: Sort descending, fill one bucket at a time with pruning; or dp over masks tracking the running remainder.
questions.alternatives: Memoised search over (mask, current bucket sum).
questions.selection_reason: The constraint size is the trigger; without reading it, the problem looks intractable.

questions.title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
questions.primary_pattern: Sliding window on the complement
questions.trigger: Removals are only from the two ends, which is not a contiguous window - but what stays behind is.
questions.why: Minimise the removed prefix+suffix by maximising the middle window summing to total-x.
questions.alternatives: Two prefix-sum hash maps from each end; DP looks plausible but is unnecessary.
questions.selection_reason: Classic restatement problem: the trigger only fires after you invert the question.

questions.title: 4Sum II
questions.primary_pattern: Meet in the middle with a hash map of pair sums
questions.trigger: Four independent arrays, so an O(n^4) enumeration splits cleanly into two halves.
questions.why: Count all sums of the first pair in a map, then look up the negation of each second-pair sum.
questions.alternatives: Sort two pair-sum arrays and two-pointer across them.
questions.selection_reason: Splitting an exponent in half is a distinct move from the usual single-pass hashing.

questions.title: Count Nice Pairs in an Array
questions.primary_pattern: Group by a rearranged key + hash map counting
questions.trigger: The pair condition a[i]+rev(a[j]) == a[j]+rev(a[i]) is symmetric, so isolate each index.
questions.why: Rearrange to a[i]-rev(a[i]) == a[j]-rev(a[j]); count equal keys and add c*(c-1)/2.
questions.alternatives: Brute force over all pairs.
questions.selection_reason: Pure 'move each index to its own side of the equation' drill from the index's pair-score line.

questions.title: Make Sum Divisible by P
questions.primary_pattern: Prefix sum modulo + hash map
questions.trigger: Remove the SHORTEST subarray so the remainder becomes divisible by p - a residue condition, not a sum condition.
questions.why: Need prefix[j]-prefix[i] = target (mod p); store the last index of each residue and look up (cur-target) mod p.
questions.alternatives: Brute force over all subarrays; two pointers, which fails because values do not bound the residue.
questions.selection_reason: Modular prefix reasoning with a negative-modulo trap - much rarer than the plain divisible-by-K version.

questions.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
questions.primary_pattern: Greedy bit-by-bit construction with a hash set (or a binary trie)
questions.trigger: Maximise a pairwise XOR without enumerating pairs.
questions.why: Build the answer from the top bit down, testing each candidate prefix against the set of masked prefixes.
questions.alternatives: Insert all numbers into a binary trie and walk the opposite branch greedily.
questions.selection_reason: Bitwise greedy where each decision is independently verifiable - a distinct mode of reasoning.

questions.title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
questions.primary_pattern: Sort + sliding window on a cost budget
questions.trigger: Budget k of increment operations, order is free, and the target must be an existing value.
questions.why: Sort, then slide a window where cost = a[r]*len - windowSum must stay <= k.
questions.alternatives: Binary search on the answer length with a prefix-sum feasibility check.
questions.selection_reason: Reads like binary search but a monotone window is simpler; strong two-approach confusion.

questions.title: Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups
questions.primary_pattern: Sweep on start/end events, or a min-heap of end times
questions.trigger: Minimum number of resources so that no two overlapping intervals share one - the classic platform count.
questions.why: The answer is the maximum number of intervals overlapping at any instant; sweep +1/-1, or greedily reuse the earliest-freeing group via a heap.
questions.alternatives: Sort by start and reuse a min-heap of end times.
questions.selection_reason: Same skeleton as meeting rooms but stated as a colouring problem, so the trigger has to be recovered.

questions.title: Stone Game VII
questions.primary_pattern: Interval DP for a two-player zero-sum game
questions.trigger: Both players play optimally from either end, so the state is the surviving interval.
questions.why: dp[i][j] = max over the two removals of (remaining sum - dp of the smaller interval).
questions.alternatives: Memoised minimax recursion on (i, j).
questions.selection_reason: Score-difference formulation is what keeps the state two-dimensional instead of exploding.

questions.title: Map of Highest Peak
questions.primary_pattern: Multi-source BFS on a grid
questions.trigger: Heights differ by at most one between neighbours, and water cells are fixed at zero.
questions.why: Push every water cell as a BFS source at once; the BFS layer number is the height.
questions.alternatives: Two-pass dynamic-programming distance transform.
questions.selection_reason: Clean instance of pushing all sources before starting - stated as a construction problem.

questions.title: Minimum Cost to Merge Stones
questions.primary_pattern: Interval DP with a K-merge residue state
questions.trigger: Merges combine K consecutive piles, so only certain interval lengths can collapse to one pile.
questions.why: dp[i][j][m] over intervals and remaining piles, splitting at steps of K-1; feasible only if (n-1) % (K-1) == 0.
questions.alternatives: Greedy min-heap merging (correct only for K=2); memoised recursion on (i, j, m).
questions.selection_reason: Deliberately collides with the heap 'combine the two smallest' trigger, which is wrong here.

questions.title: Shortest Unsorted Continuous Subarray
questions.primary_pattern: Prefix maximum and suffix minimum scans
questions.trigger: Find the shortest window whose sorting fixes the whole array.
questions.why: The right edge is the last index where prefixMax > a[i]; the left edge is the first where suffixMin < a[i].
questions.alternatives: Sort a copy and compare boundaries; monotonic stack from both sides.
questions.selection_reason: Two-directional scanning where the naive sort-and-diff answer hides the O(n) structure.

questions.title: Form Largest Integer With Digits That Add up to Target
questions.primary_pattern: Unbounded knapsack + lexicographic reconstruction
questions.trigger: Digits are reusable with fixed costs and an exact budget, and the answer is the largest NUMBER.
questions.why: dp[t] = the maximum number of digits for cost t, then rebuild greedily from digit 9 downwards.
questions.alternatives: Direct string-DP comparison with a custom bigger-number comparator.
questions.selection_reason: Unbounded knapsack whose objective is lexicographic, which breaks naive value comparison.

questions.title: Replace the Substring for Balanced String
questions.primary_pattern: Variable sliding window with an outside-the-window condition
questions.trigger: You may rewrite one substring arbitrarily; feasibility depends on the characters NOT in the window.
questions.why: Shrink the smallest window such that every count outside it is <= n/4.
questions.alternatives: Binary search on window length plus a check; greedy fails.
questions.selection_reason: Inverts the usual window invariant - the condition lives outside the window.

questions.title: Minimize the Maximum of Two Arrays
questions.primary_pattern: Binary search on the answer + inclusion-exclusion with LCM
questions.trigger: The answer space reaches 10^9 while the check is pure counting - the array can never be built.
questions.why: Count how many values <= x are usable by each array using multiples of the divisors and their LCM, then binary search.
questions.alternatives: Greedy construction; direct simulation (impossible at this size).
questions.selection_reason: Joins the huge-answer-space signal with LCM counting - two index sections in one problem.

questions.title: Advantage Shuffle
questions.primary_pattern: Greedy matching after sorting both sides
questions.trigger: Maximise the count of positions where you beat the opponent; your order is completely free.
questions.why: Sort both; for each opponent value spend the smallest card that beats it, otherwise dump your weakest.
questions.alternatives: Multiset with upper_bound lookups per opponent value.
questions.selection_reason: The 'advantage' framing hides a standard sorted-greedy pairing, and the dump-the-weakest step is easy to miss.

questions.title: Super Pow
questions.primary_pattern: Fast modular exponentiation with an array exponent
questions.trigger: The exponent is given as a digit array, so it cannot be reconstructed as an integer.
questions.why: Apply a^(10d + r) = (a^d)^10 * a^r digit by digit, with binary exponentiation modulo 1337.
questions.alternatives: Euler's theorem to reduce the exponent modulo phi(1337).
questions.selection_reason: The exponent's SIZE is the trigger - the index's 'input cannot be iterated' signal, in miniature.

questions.title: Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended
questions.primary_pattern: Sweep by day + min-heap of end days
questions.trigger: One event per day, each with a window - the classic 'sort by end' greedy no longer fits directly.
questions.why: Advance day by day, push events that have started, discard expired ones, and attend the earliest-ending.
questions.alternatives: Union-find over the next free day.
questions.selection_reason: Bridges interval greedy and heap scheduling, with a natural union-find alternative.

questions.title: Find Eventual Safe States
questions.primary_pattern: Cycle detection via DFS colouring, or reverse-graph topological sort
questions.trigger: A node is safe iff no path from it reaches a cycle.
questions.why: Three-colour DFS marking nodes in the recursion stack, or Kahn's algorithm on the reversed graph.
questions.alternatives: Iterative topological sort on reversed edges by out-degree.
questions.selection_reason: Directed cycle detection where the answer is the complement of what the DFS naturally finds.

questions.title: Count Number of Nice Subarrays
questions.primary_pattern: Prefix count + hash map (or atMost window)
questions.trigger: Counts subarrays containing exactly k odd numbers - parity turns into a prefix count.
questions.why: Treat odd as 1, then it is 'subarrays summing to k' via a prefix-count map.
questions.alternatives: atMost(k) - atMost(k-1) with a window; gap counting between odd positions.
questions.selection_reason: Cleanly bridges the window and prefix-sum families on the same statement.

questions.title: Path With Minimum Effort
questions.primary_pattern: Binary search on the answer + BFS, or Dijkstra on a minimax path
questions.trigger: Minimise the maximum edge weight along a path - a minimax route rather than a sum.
questions.why: Either binary search the threshold and BFS through allowed edges, or run Dijkstra where the cost is a running max.
questions.alternatives: Kruskal-style union-find, adding edges by weight until start and end connect.
questions.selection_reason: Three legitimate patterns fit; deciding between them is the exercise.

questions.title: Count Subarrays Where Max Element Appears at Least K Times
questions.primary_pattern: Sliding window counting subarrays
questions.trigger: 'At least K occurrences' plus 'count all subarrays' - a monotone property once the max is fixed.
questions.why: Slide right, shrink while the count of the global max is >= k, add left as the number of valid starts.
questions.alternatives: Prefix positions of the max element plus index arithmetic.
questions.selection_reason: Teaches the 'add left+1 to the answer' counting idiom rather than length maximisation.

questions.title: Score of Parentheses
questions.primary_pattern: Stack of partial scores
questions.trigger: Nested structure where an inner result is combined into its enclosing frame.
questions.why: Push 0 on '(', and on ')' fold the top as max(2*top, 1) into the frame below.
questions.alternatives: Count only the depth of each '()' pair and sum 2^depth.
questions.selection_reason: Small statement that separates real stack reasoning from mere bracket matching.

questions.title: Maximum Length of Subarray With Positive Product
questions.primary_pattern: Linear DP carrying two running lengths
questions.trigger: Sign, not magnitude, decides validity, and a single negative flips the whole product.
questions.why: Carry the longest positive-product and longest negative-product suffix lengths, resetting at zeros.
questions.alternatives: Split at zeros and use the first/last negative index in each segment.
questions.selection_reason: Looks like a sliding window and is not - the state has to survive sign flips.

questions.title: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
questions.primary_pattern: Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest paths
questions.trigger: n <= 100 with all-pairs reachability under a distance threshold - the size explicitly permits O(n^3).
questions.why: Run Floyd-Warshall, then count reachable cities per node under the threshold.
questions.alternatives: Dijkstra from every node.
questions.selection_reason: The clearest case of the constraint table choosing the algorithm before any thinking.

questions.title: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination
questions.primary_pattern: Dijkstra carrying a path count alongside the distance
questions.trigger: Not just the shortest time, but HOW MANY shortest routes achieve it, modulo 1e9+7.
questions.why: During relaxation, reset the count on a strict improvement and add on an equal-distance tie.
questions.alternatives: Dijkstra first, then a DAG DP over the shortest-path graph.
questions.selection_reason: Extends a known algorithm with counting - the tie-handling detail is the real test.

questions.title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
questions.primary_pattern: Sliding window (exactly-K via atMost)
questions.trigger: Counts contiguous subarrays with EXACTLY K distinct values; a single variable window cannot hold an exact-count invariant.
questions.why: exactly(K) = atMost(K) - atMost(K-1); each atMost is a standard shrinking window.
questions.alternatives: Two-pointer with two synchronized left bounds; brute force O(n^2) with counts.
questions.selection_reason: Forces the subtractive decomposition, the single most transferable window trick.

questions.title: Recover Binary Search Tree
questions.primary_pattern: In-order traversal invariant + swapped-pair detection
questions.trigger: Exactly two nodes are swapped, and in-order must be strictly increasing.
questions.why: Track the previous node during in-order; the first and last violations identify the swapped pair.
questions.alternatives: Morris traversal for O(1) space; collect the in-order list and diff it against its sorted copy.
questions.selection_reason: Uses the BST ordering property as a detector rather than as a search rule.

questions.title: Maximum Population Year
questions.primary_pattern: Difference array over a small coordinate domain
questions.trigger: Intervals of years, and you need the point with maximum coverage - the domain is tiny.
questions.why: Increment at birth, decrement at death, prefix-sum the timeline, take the argmax.
questions.alternatives: Sort start/end events and sweep with a counter.
questions.selection_reason: Rare Easy where the trigger (range coverage, not the intervals themselves) is the whole problem.

questions.title: Binary Tree Cameras
questions.primary_pattern: Post-order DFS with a three-state return + greedy placement
questions.trigger: Minimise placed nodes under a covering constraint that reaches one level in each direction.
questions.why: Return NEEDS_COVER / HAS_CAMERA / COVERED from each child and place a camera only when a child needs one.
questions.alternatives: dp[node][3] tree DP over the same three states.
questions.selection_reason: Greedy and DP both work; deriving the state set from the covering radius is the exercise.

questions.title: Maximum Alternating Subsequence Sum
questions.primary_pattern: State-machine DP with two carried states
questions.trigger: Each element is taken at an even or odd position, or skipped - a tiny state set carried forward.
questions.why: Track best sums ending on an even index and on an odd index; each element updates both.
questions.alternatives: Greedy sum of positive consecutive differences.
questions.selection_reason: Pure structural twin of the buy/sell state machine without any of its familiarity.

questions.title: Minimum Deletions to Make Character Frequencies Unique
questions.primary_pattern: Frequency counting + greedy decrement into free slots
questions.trigger: All frequencies must become distinct, and only deletions are allowed.
questions.why: Sort frequencies descending and lower each one until it hits an unused value, accumulating the drops.
questions.alternatives: Track used counts in a hash set while scanning frequencies.
questions.selection_reason: Small greedy whose exchange argument (always lower the larger) is worth stating explicitly.

questions.title: Best Sightseeing Pair
questions.primary_pattern: Rearrange a pair score, carry the best left contribution
questions.trigger: Score is values[i]+values[j]+i-j with i<j - the index distance is baked into the score.
questions.why: Split into (values[i]+i) and (values[j]-j); scan right, keeping the best left term seen so far.
questions.alternatives: O(n^2) pair enumeration; a monotonic-stack framing.
questions.selection_reason: Literal instance of the index's 'contribution from left + contribution from right' line.

questions.title: Grouping
questions.primary_pattern: Bitmask DP over subsets with submask enumeration
questions.trigger: Partition N <= 16 items into groups with a pairwise score - N is tiny, which permits exponential state.
questions.why: Precompute the score of every subset, then dp[mask] = max over submasks of dp[mask ^ sub] + score[sub], enumerated as sub = (sub-1) & mask.
questions.alternatives: Greedy grouping (wrong); brute force over all set partitions (Bell numbers, too slow).
questions.selection_reason: Covers the index's 'partition into groups, small N' line with true submask enumeration, which LeetCode's bitmask problems rarely require.

questions.title: Dungeon Game
questions.primary_pattern: Grid DP computed BACKWARDS from the destination
questions.trigger: The requirement at a cell depends on future cells, so a forward prefix cannot decide it.
questions.why: dp[i][j] = max(1, min(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1]) - grid[i][j]), filled from the bottom-right.
questions.alternatives: Binary search the starting health with a forward feasibility DP.
questions.selection_reason: Direct drill on the index's 'loop direction opposite to the recursion' rule.

questions.title: Last Stone Weight II
questions.primary_pattern: Subset sum / 0-1 knapsack in disguise
questions.trigger: Every stone ends up with a + or - sign, so the answer is the smallest achievable |difference|.
questions.why: Minimise |total - 2*S| over reachable subset sums S; a boolean knapsack over total/2.
questions.alternatives: Greedy heap simulation (wrong); meet in the middle.
questions.selection_reason: Reads like the heap simulation of its own prequel; the restatement is the entire problem.
